headline: Biological priors inform models predicting expression from histology and perturbations
label: Biology Informed Machine Learning
summary: Foundation models and graph-based architectures now encode tissue, spatial, and perturbation context to predict transcriptomic and proteomic states.
synthesis: The dominant thread is external biological knowledge injected into models of tissue and single-cell data. BCARP applies biology-guided residual propagation to H&E-derived spatial expression predictions, and ALHENA distills transcriptomic foundation model knowledge into an H&E encoder trained on paired Xenium data. Distillation recurs elsewhere: scAnyOmics transfers a frozen single-cell foundation model into a multimodal student for any-to-any RNA, protein, and ATAC completion. RFind-sc projects cells onto axes defined by external gene signatures, Kontext couples cells with local environments through ligand-receptor interactions, and EMBER uses frozen contextualized gene embeddings. What appears new is cross-modal transfer, in which histology alone is used to infer transcriptomic, spatial, or single-cell readouts. The items are heterogeneous and most report item-specific benchmarks, so cross-study comparison remains limited.
